subject: Energy
title: The 10,000-Year Warning Problem
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: The 10,000-Year Warning Problem.

hook.text: How do you warn future humans to stay away from buried nuclear waste—when no language lasts 10,000 years?

buildup.text: Written language is only about 5,000 years old—any message we write today may be unreadable by then.

discovery.text: Proposals include hostile architecture (menacing spike fields), ray cats that glow near radiation, and folklore.

twist.text: Some experts argue the best strategy is to forget—deep burial in stable geology works whether people know or not.

climax.text: Finland's approach is simple: bury it deep, seal it, and let the rock do the work for 100,000+ years.

punchline.text: How to say 'danger' in a language that doesn't exist yet.

quiz.question: Why is warning future generations about nuclear waste so difficult?
